title: Security Classification, Privacy Markings & Copy Numbering
source: Defence Forces Service Writing Manual 2024 (JP-04), Chapter 2
notes: Security rules are amplified by single-Service security publications; these are the basic checks.

rules.title: Security classification must be one of the four recognised grades
rules.description: The four security classifications are TOP SECRET, SECRET, CONFIDENTIAL and RESTRICTED.

rules.title: Security classification shown at top and bottom of pages
rules.description: The security classification is shown at the top and bottom of the front and back covers and on every page (for loose-leaf) or at centre top and bottom of covers, title page, first and last pages (for securely bound documents).

check.where: Header and footer of each page.

rules.title: Document must be graded at least as high as its most classified component
rules.description: The grading of a main paper must be at least as high as that of its most classified component, and a file or group of related documents must be graded as the highest graded document within it.

check.where: Comparison of document grade with annex/appendix grades.

rules.title: Privacy marking 'IN CONFIDENCE' shown at top and bottom of every page
rules.description: Documents requiring privacy protection are endorsed 'IN CONFIDENCE' (optionally prefixed, e.g. 'STAFF IN CONFIDENCE'), shown at the top and bottom of every page and stamped in red ink.

check.where: Header and footer of each page.

rules.title: TOP SECRET and SECRET documents bear copy numbers
rules.description: All TOP SECRET and SECRET documents bear individual copy numbers, e.g. 'Copy No 1 of 20 copies', in the top right hand corner of the first page and on each classified annex, appendix or trace.

check.where: Top right of the first page.

rules.title: Operation and administrative/logistics orders are copy numbered
rules.description: All operation and administrative/logistics orders, whatever their security classification, are given a copy number.

check.where: Top right of the first page of orders.

rules.notes: Applies to operation orders, admin/log orders (Chapter 12/14 documents).

rules.title: Copy number format must be 'Copy No X of Y copies'
rules.description: When one copy exists it is shown as 'Copy No 1 of 1 copy'. Reproduction copies are marked 'REPRODUCTION Copy No... Of... Copies'.

rules.title: TOP SECRET/SECRET pages show total page count
rules.description: In TOP SECRET and SECRET documents and classified documents bearing supplementary international markings, all pages are numbered to indicate the total number of pages, e.g. '1 of 20'.

rules.title: Annex pages are numbered with the annex letter
rules.description: Pages of an annex, including a single-page annex, are given the letter of the annex followed by the page number, e.g. 'A-1', 'A-2'. Annexes following chapters use '1A-1', '1A-2'. Appendix pages use e.g. '5B4-2'.

check.where: Page numbers of annexes and appendices.

rules.title: Precedence marking shown in capitals at top right of the first page only
rules.description: The precedence marking (IMMEDIATE or PRIORITY) is shown in capital letters at the top right of the first page only.

check.where: Top right of the first page.

rules.title: IMMEDIATE precedence requires senior authority
rules.description: Authorization of IMMEDIATE precedence is normally confined to senior staff officers and commanders of independent units; any commissioned officer can originate PRIORITY papers.
